title: Mexico’s Culture Ministry Announces Mass Book Purchase for the National Library Network
author: Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by[Alonso
Urrutia](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alonso%20Urrutia,%20enviado)
originally appeared in the [September 18, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/18/cultura/cultura-
anuncia-compra-masiva-de-libros-para-la-red-nacional-de-bibliotecas), Mexico's
premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Irapuato, Guanajuato**. After reaffirming the importance of the **sales-tax
exemption for bookstores** (a zero VAT rate), which is included in the 2027
economic package, with an annual benefit of 200 million pesos for the sector,
the Secretary of Culture, Claudia Curiel de Icaza, announced that on Monday
they will launch a call for the mass purchase of books for the national
library network, for an amount of **50 million pesos**.

> Mexican, independent and mid-sized publishers will of course be able to
> participate, and this will also nourish this network of libraries for the
> benefit of the reader.
>
> Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture

She maintained that the zero rate is fundamental to strengthening the
ecosystem of the book and of readers. "Publishers had support from this rate
more than twenty-odd years ago, but there was no support for distribution, and
that generated a significant asymmetry." So, the zero rate "would help them
deduct operating expenses, the bookstore networks are going to be
strengthened, and it implies an annual benefit of around 200 million pesos for
this sector."

She stressed that the initiative arises after more than 20 years of demand.
"It is an initiative on the part of the Chamber of the Mexican Publishing
Industry, Paco Ignacio Taibo, the Brigada para Leer en Libertad, and it is a
very important demand."

At the mañanera, she noted that the two actions are important because they
strengthen distribution, bookstores—also considered cultural
infrastructure—and national publishers.

She noted that, in collaboration between the Secretariat of Culture and the
Fondo de Cultura Económica, there are **26,000 reading clubs and reading
rooms** , with the goal of reaching around **250,000 participants** by the end
of the year. She recalled that the Cervantino Festival will take place from
October 3 to 18, with more than 200 activities in Celaya and León, Guanajuato.
